<SUMMARY>The week of June 5-12, 2026, was characterized by intensified geopolitical maneuvering in the AI and critical minerals sectors, coupled with significant developments in regional conflicts and defense postures. President Donald Trump claimed a "great settlement" had been reached with Iran, even as Israel continued to violate the Gaza ceasefire. Export controls gained prominence, with Republican lawmakers urging the U.S. ITC to block TSMC chip imports and the U.S. Senate weighing new legislation targeting chips and AI. China implemented export curbs on tungsten, while the Democratic Republic of Congo initiated a cobalt export ban, further straining critical mineral supply chains. Major investments in AI infrastructure, including SpaceX's record IPO and large-scale data center developments, underscore the accelerating global AI race amidst heightened energy demands.</SUMMARY>
<EWS>The potential U.S. ITC block on foreign-made TSMC chips, as urged by Republican lawmakers, indicates a direct threat to global chip supply. China’s export curbs on tungsten pose a risk to Japan’s AI chip supply chain. Taiwan is weighing tighter rules for AI chip exports to China, further tightening the global tech landscape. The Democratic Republic of Congo's cobalt export ban spells trouble for the EV battery supply. The European Union’s 21st sanctions package, which includes Indian entities, threatens to complicate the ratification of the EU-India trade agreement. Israel's continued violations of the Gaza ceasefire, resulting in 13 deaths in a single day, highlight ongoing regional instability. The prospect of water infrastructure targeting in the Third Gulf War suggests a potential humanitarian crisis.</EWS>
<EXEC>

**Asia:**
Chinese authorities arrested an American scholar on suspicion of espionage. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman canceled a planned trip to Korea amid cooling chip work with Samsung.

**Europe:**
Mistral AI seeks to raise €3 billion at a €20 billion valuation. Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan won re-election, maintaining the country's Western trajectory. Europe's race to secure power for data centers and electrification projects has led customers to pay extra to secure spots in gas turbine production queues, according to Siemens Energy AG.

**Americas:**
Elon Musk’s SpaceX went public, raising $75 billion. Aymer AI announced the formation of a strategic venture to develop a 90-acre powered land bank in Texas, designed for large-scale AI data centers. LIXTE Biotechnology Holdings, Inc. is reinventing itself as a power-infrastructure company, aimed at addressing the electricity shortage throttling the AI sector. Microsoft restricted employees' access to Claude Fable 5 due to data retention policies.

**Oceania:**
Sharon AI announced a six-year strategic compute collaboration with Nvidia, which will support the rollout of 72 megawatts of new data centers.</EXEC>
<LITHO>

**Asia:**
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stated that AI has become "insanely profitable" for Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM) during COMPUTEX 2026 in Taiwan. Republican members of Congress urged the U.S. ITC to block imports of foreign-made chips, specifically TSMC chips, found to infringe U.S. patents asserted by United Microelectronics Corporation. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman cancelled his Korea trip as chip work with Samsung cools down. Taiwan weighs tighter rules for AI chip exports to China. Korean AI ETFs and Taiwanese options offer direct exposure to the AI supply chain.

**Americas:**
Bechtel will build the first phase of construction on Micron’s $100 billion semiconductor plant in the U.S. Bangladesh secured semiconductor partnerships with Intel, Synopsys, and SanDisk during a U.S. roadshow.

**Europe:**
A Chinese startup claims photonic chip production without DUV lithography using a nanoimprint process, stating it cuts costs by 90% and produces 8-inch wafers without conventional optical lithography. Europe is pursuing a new AI chip dream.</LITHO>
<REE>

**Asia:**
China controls a pivotal "AI chokepoint" in rare earth elements processing, specifically a near-total monopoly of approximately 90% globally. China’s export curbs on tungsten threaten Japan’s AI chip supply chain.

**Africa:**
The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) implemented a cobalt export ban, signaling potential trouble for the world's EV battery supply chain. A rare meteorite recovered from the Sahara Desert could be a fragment of a Moon-size body.

**Americas:**
The U.S. House of Representatives passed H.R. 7037, the DOMINANCE Act, a bipartisan bill aimed at dismantling China’s near-total monopoly on the global processing of rare earth elements. The Boundary Waters wilderness in northeastern Minnesota is at risk from a "clean energy" mine. Montana's history is shaped by its minerals. MAX Power's shareholders completed a warrant exercise totaling $3.75 million.

**Europe:**
Metso invested in new mineralogy analysis equipment in Finland, installing a TESCAN TIMA automated mineralogy analyser at its research facility.</REE>
<GEO>

**Asia:**
Republican lawmakers urged the U.S. ITC to block imports of foreign-made TSMC chips found to infringe U.S. patents. China implemented export curbs on tungsten. Taiwan is weighing tighter rules for AI chip exports to China.

**Americas:**
The Senate Banking Committee is weighing markup of export control legislation targeting chips and AI. The U.S. House of Representatives passed H.R. 7037, the DOMINANCE Act, to counter China’s rare earth monopoly.

**Europe:**
The European Union’s 21st sanctions package against Russia includes entities based in India, a move that could complicate ratification of a trade agreement finalized between Brussels and New Delhi in January.</GEO>
<MILITARY>

**Asia:**
The Philippines and Canada signed a Mutual Logistics Support Arrangement (MLSA), boosting defense cooperation.

**Americas:**
Avtandil Kalandadze, 47, the former ship master of a ghost fleet tanker that transported Iran- and Venezuela-origin oil, pleaded guilty in U.S. District Court in D.C. for refusing to obey orders from the U.S. Coast Guard during a weeks-long pursuit. SpaceX’s IPO has implications for space commerce and extraterrestrial exploration. BQP appointed NUAIR CEO Craig Marcinkowski to its Board of Directors as U.S. growth accelerates across defense and aerospace.

**Oceania:**
Missile defense systems worked against Iran, but may not work against China.</MILITARY>
<CONCLUSION>The convergence of geopolitical tensions, particularly regarding critical resources and technological supremacy, continues to drive strategic realignments and significant investments. The escalating competition in AI and semiconductor sectors, coupled with persistent regional conflicts and a renewed focus on energy security, defines the current global landscape.</CONCLUSION>
<INDIA>Electric two-wheeler maker Ultraviolette is expecting a 5X growth in exports this financial year, with exports accounting for about 10% of the company’s business. NLC India Limited was declared the preferred bidder for the Parvathapur Vanadium, Titanium, and Aluminous Laterite block in Telangana, secured through an e-auction conducted by the Ministry of Mines. The European Union’s 21st sanctions package against Russia includes entities based in India, a move that could complicate the ratification of a trade agreement finalized between Brussels and New Delhi in January. Indian benchmark indices surged nearly 2%, with Sensex rising 1,695 points and Nifty gaining 461 points, driven by broad-based buying, banking sector strength, and easing crude oil prices following improved global geopolitical sentiment.</INDIA>
<WEST_ASIA>OpenAI CEO Sam Altman cancelled his Abu Dhabi trip amid tensions, potentially hindering OpenAI's Middle East expansion. US President Donald Trump claimed a "great settlement" has been reached with Iran to end the Middle East war, stating the agreement could be signed as early as this weekend, possibly in Europe, though Iran stated this is not so. Israel continued to violate the Gaza ceasefire, killing 13 people in a single day and over 1,000 people since the ceasefire took effect in October 2025. The U.S. government escorted oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz at night. King Faisal Specialist Hospital & Research Centre (KFSH) in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, will highlight the strategic value of tertiary care AI datasets at HLTH Europe 2026. The Iran War may be permanently rewiring global energy security. Qatar pursued secret talks with Iran to shield its gas complex from strikes, according to security officials. The bombing of water infrastructure and possible escalation towards desalinization plants in the Third Gulf War could generate the greatest humanitarian crisis in decades. Easing concerns over tensions in the Middle East and a strong rally in U.S. technology shares fueled broad buying, leading the Nikkei Stock Average to close back above the 66,000 level. Japan aims to boost cooperation on economic security, including energy, through Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's visit to Europe amid the Middle East conflict. SCC Middle East's move will bolster AI knowledge.</WEST_ASIA>
<FINAL_CONCLUSION>The coming period will likely see persistent geopolitical tensions driven by the accelerating global AI race, critical resource competition, and efforts to redefine international trade and security architectures. The interplay of export controls, strategic investments in advanced technology, and evolving regional conflicts will continue to shape global stability and economic landscapes.</FINAL_CONCLUSION>
